questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Integration of Princely States' refers to.
questions.a: At independence in 1947, India had over 500 princely states. Integration was the process by which these states acceded to the Indian Union, forming a unified nation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Integration of Princely States'.
questions.a: Most princely states joined India through persuasion and agreements; a few required special measures.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Integration of Princely States'.
questions.a: explain the process of integration of princely states

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'States Reorganisation Act 1956' refers to.
questions.a: The States Reorganisation Act 1956 was a law that reorganised the boundaries of Indian states on the basis of language, reducing the number of states and creating a more rational administrative structure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'States Reorganisation Act 1956'.
questions.a: The Act redrew state boundaries primarily along linguistic lines, replacing the earlier arrangement inherited from British rule.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'States Reorganisation Act 1956'.
questions.a: explain the purpose of the States Reorganisation Act 1956

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Formation of Linguistic States' refers to.
questions.a: Linguistic states are states organised so that people speaking a common language form a single administrative unit. Andhra Pradesh was the first linguistic state, formed in 1953 after the fasting death of Potti Sriramulu.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Formation of Linguistic States'.
questions.a: Creating linguistic states made administration easier and strengthened democratic participation by respecting language identity.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Formation of Linguistic States'.
questions.a: explain how Andhra Pradesh became the first linguistic state

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Boundary Changes and Their Reasons' refers to.
questions.a: Boundary changes are alterations to the borders of states or creation of new states to improve administration, address linguistic or cultural identity, or meet regional demands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Boundary Changes and Their Reasons'.
questions.a: Boundaries change over time due to linguistic demands, administrative convenience, and regional movements.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Boundary Changes and Their Reasons'.
questions.a: explain reasons for boundary changes in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Union Territories' refers to.
questions.a: Union Territories are regions administered directly by the Central Government of India. They do not have the full powers of a state and are governed by an administrator or Lieutenant Governor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Union Territories'.
questions.a: Union Territories are created for strategic, cultural, or administrative reasons where direct central control is preferred.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Union Territories'.
questions.a: define Union Territory

questions.q: Using the method 'Administrative Divisions of India', work with: states = 40, uts = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of count.
questions.a: 48 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Administrative Divisions of India' and work with: states = 25, uts = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of count.
questions.a: 265 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Administrative Divisions of India' refers to.
questions.a: India is administratively divided into states and Union Territories. States are further divided into districts, and districts into tehsils or blocks for governance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Administrative Divisions of India'.
questions.a: The administrative hierarchy flows from the Centre to states to districts to local bodies, enabling governance at each level.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Administrative Divisions of India', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_units = states + union_territories

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Current Political Map of India' refers to.
questions.a: The current political map of India shows 28 states and 8 Union Territories, reflecting the latest boundary changes including the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Current Political Map of India'.
questions.a: The political map changes with the creation of new states and Union Territories; the latest major change was in 2019 with Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Current Political Map of India'.
questions.a: identify states on the political map of India
